title: nvlink + libinterposer reproducibility diary
content:
TL;DR:
Had a recurring OOM (CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY) during large-batch inference when an LD_PRELOAD-based interposer was present and NVLink links were active between GPU pairs. Suspect symbol conflict / double-free between interposer and driver-provided libcuda/nvidia libraries. Repro is flaky; this doc is a running diary of commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and next experiments.

Context / why this matters:
- A customer-facing Dedicated fleet uses an internal interposer (LD_PRELOAD) to capture allocation metadata and inject debug hooks.
- Intermittent VM-level OOMs correlate with large KV-cache workloads (~40B token sequences).
- When NVLink enabled between adjacent cards, OOMs spike; with NVLink disabled, much more stable.

Environment matrix (tested so far):
- GPUs: NVIDIA A100-40GB (pci ids 0000:65:00.0 / 0000:66:00.0), also quick check on A40 (non-repro).
- Drivers: 525.85.12, 535.86.05 (both repro windows but different probabilities).
- CUDA toolkits: 11.8, 12.1 (containers built for both).
- Container runtime: docker + nvidia-container-toolkit 1.11.0; also repro inside systemd-nspawn (weirdly less flaky).
- Interposer: /opt/interposer/libinterpose.so (LD_PRELOAD). Version: 0.9.12 (dev build).
- Workload: batched generation with KV-cache enabled, batch size 48, seq_len up to 4096.

Repro command (minimal-ish):
- docker run --gpus all -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 -e LD_PRELOAD=/opt/interposer/libinterpose.so 
  --rm -it rwdw/infer-test:cuda12 bash -c "python repro_alloc.py --batch 48 --seq 4096 --steps 200"

Observed error snippets (collected across runs):
- Python-level: CUDA out of memory: Tried to allocate 1.63 GiB (error message: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY)
- low-level libcudart: CUDART: cudart returned error 2 at src/alloc.c:142
- Kernel/NVRM: NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed!; NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=12345, name="python"
- dmesg: [ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (0000:65:00): 79, pid 12345, GPU has fallen off the bus
- ldpreload mix: warning: symbol collision: libinterpose.so defines cudaMalloc; overriding libcuda.so.

Commands tried (notes):
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -i 0/1 -> confirmed free/used numbers spike before crash
- ldd /opt/interposer/libinterpose.so -> shows it links to libdl, libpthread only; uses dlsym(RTLD_NEXT) to wrap libcalls
- LD_DEBUG=bindings python repro_alloc.py -> printed messages indicating multiple bindings to cudaMalloc/cuMemAlloc
- LD_PRELOAD unset -> problem rarely repros (almost stable)
- nvlink status: nvidia-smi topo -m shows NVLink between 0 <-> 1 active for A100 pair; forcing NVLink off with nvidia-smi topo -k not possible but physically removing link (on test rig) stops repro
- strace -f -e trace=open,close,mmap,mprotect -p <pid> during run -> saw mmap failures around /dev/nvidia0 shortly before crash
- sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version -> different kernel module versions on nodes that repro vs nodes that don't (kernel module 535.86.05 vs 525.85.12)
- ran gdb server attach and bt on crashed python process in a few cases: stack shows cudaDriverGetVersion -> cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain -> cuMemAlloc -> [libinterpose.so: wrapped_cudaMalloc] -> free -> double-free pattern sometimes visible

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) LD_PRELOAD interposer hooks a subset of allocation/free symbols but misses newer symbol names in driver 535, causing both interposer and driver to attempt free/cleanup -> double-free -> heap corruption -> OOM-like behavior.
2) NVLink introduces remote-mapped pages / peer-to-peer mappings. The interposer's bookkeeping assumes local allocations only and gets confused when memory is pinned for NVLink transfers, leaking or double-freeing entries in our kvcache.
3) Driver ABI drift between 525 and 535 means different internal calls (e.g., cuMemAlloc_v2 vs cuMemAlloc) so our wrappers are incompatible.
4) Race introduced by delayed kernel events with NVLink where the interposer's destructor runs during an async DMA completion; ordering causes free of still-in-use page.

Small experiments and outcomes: (quick bullets)
- Recompile interposer with full symbol coverage (added cuMemAlloc_v2, cuMemFree_v2) -> lowered failure rate but still saw OOMs under long runs (suggests more than just symbol name mismatch).
- Disable peer-to-peer (nvidia-smi --p2p 0) -> repro rate drops to near-zero in our test rack. Good signal that NVLink/p2p is involved.
- Add explicit cudaDeviceSynchronize() before free in the wrapper -> immediate reduction in crashes in 3/4 runs (supports async free/race hypothesis).
- Run with driver 525 only -> almost no repro; with driver 535 almost always repro. So driver-related change is gating factor.

Important logs (raw snippets copied):
- Python trace:
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/torch/cuda/memory.py", line 420, in _malloc
  raise OutOfMemoryError("CUDA out of memory")
  torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 175,327,232 bytes

- dmesg around event:
  [ 3212.312341] NVRM: Xid (0000:65:00): 79, pid 16521, name="python"
  [ 3212.312412] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus

- LD_PRELOAD debug output (added prints):
  [libinterpose] wrap: cuMemAlloc(0xA500000) -> returned CUresult 0x0 at 0x7f9d4c
  [libinterpose] free: cuMemFree(addr=0x7f9c1234) -> scheduling delayed free (async)
  [libinterpose] destructor: flushing delayed frees (found 2 entries)
  [libinterpose] WARNING: trying to free addr 0x7f9c1234 but not found in table (double free?)

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there driver-side callbacks invoked for NVLink transfer completion that interpose should be aware of?
- Does the kernel module in 535 change the mapping semantics such that the same pointer can be freed from different contexts?
- Why does systemd-nspawn show lower flakiness vs docker on same node? cgroup or ipc namespace differences?

Next experiments (planned):
- Minimal C repro: write tiny C program that allocs + peer-to-peer copy across NVLink with/without LD_PRELOAD wrapper (aim to remove Python/Torch noise). Capture with cuda-memcheck and run 50k iterations.
- Run with instrumented driver symbols via LD_PRELOAD to log all cu* calls to a file (huge volume, will need sampling).
- Try building interposer to use RTLD_NEXT only for libc calls and avoid wrapping any libcuda symbols; instead use cuMemGetAddressRange hooks (if available) to observe allocations without intervening.
- Ask platform team to repro on fresh nodes with driver 535 but different kernel minor (to see if kernel module build-time options matter).
- Add a short-lifetime test that toggles NVLink off/on (if hardware allows) to observe immediate correlation.

Notes to self (manual steps / commands to re-run quickly):
- docker run --gpus device=0,1 -e LD_PRELOAD=/opt/interposer/libinterpose.so rwdw/infer-test 
- sudo dmesg -T | grep -i nvrm -A4 -B4
- LD_DEBUG=bindings python repro_alloc.py 2>&1 | tee /tmp/ldbinds.log
- perf record -e sys_enter_mmap -a -o perf-mmap.data sleep 60 (during repro)

Slack links / people to ping: 
- #gpu-ops: @ethan (Ethan Park) saw a similar pattern in March 2026 on a different fleet.
- Infra: @maya (Maya Rodriguez) for driver rollbacks and test node provisioning.

Decision log / quick mitigations we've tested and outcomes:
- Immediate workaround: unset LD_PRELOAD for production jobs touching NVLink-enabled cards -> stops the interposer telemetry but stabilizes fleet (temporary).
- Medium-term: ship interposer update that is conservative (no direct wrap of cuMem*; only record via secondary inspection) -> currently in review (PR linked above).

If stuck, escalation plan:
1) Capture kernel dump + full nv-hosttrace during a failing run, open SR with NVIDIA if we can reproduce on demand.
2) If reproducible, propose a small microbenchmark to NVIDIA engineering that shows P2P + LD_PRELOAD-induced crash.

Misc observations (random):
- On one node, enabling persistence daemon (nvidia-persistenced) reduced frequency; maybe ordering of driver init matters.
- I saw a single case where the app reported OOM but GPUs still had free memory -> suggests corruption of bookkeeping (my code or driver).

Conclusion so far: Strong correlation between NVLink/p2p + interposer + driver >=535. Practical mitigation is to avoid LD_PRELOAD on NVLink-enabled production workloads until we have a safe interposer variant.

Next entry TODO: add C minimal repro, attach reproducer link, try patch that defers frees until explicit cudaDeviceSynchronize().

END OF NOTE (2026-03-10)
